column1: # The longest sound in the game, heard on both sides.
# `audio.md §8.2`: the Stonegate trapdoor's scripted death plays "every integer
# frequency from 1000 down through 251 Hz, 750 tones total, holding each for 40
# calibrated units", then one 75-update rumble per party member as that member
# is killed. Section 10 marks the sweep's ~26.5 s duration as **derived and
# unverified** - "far longer than the effect intuitively sounds" - so this is
# the capture that settles it.
# The trapdoor is a ring of eight cells around Stonegate's centre; the seed
# stands in the middle, so one step in any direction lands on it. Each side is
# driven separately, and each recording is preceded by a silence control.
# not-a-comparison: the two sides step onto the trapdoor forty seconds apart
# This is an audio scenario, and its structure is the A/B stagger: the engine
# steps, forty seconds are captured, and only then does DOSBox step and get
# its own forty. That is right for a sound capture and wrong for the message
# window, because the step starts a minute-long cinematic. At `dosbox-fallen`
# the DOSBox side is forty seconds into its rescue and the engine side is
# eighty seconds into one it has already finished, so the two windows are
# never at the same beat and the comparator's staggered-beat rule - which
# assumes the second shot of a pair has both sides in the same state - does
# not hold here.
# The window is compared by `stonegate-rescue-pacing`, which steps both sides
# together and agrees on all seventeen samples.
# requires-seed: the party inside Stonegate, standing in the trapdoor ring's centre cell
# Fixed 2026-09-12. `town-mode.md` line 148's scripted death kills the party,
# and the capability check then reaches `blackthorn.md` §7's rescue/refuge
# cinematic on both sides. This engine used to print only the `KARMA.DAT`
# verdict, because §7's contract list names the beats by role. The literals
# are published in the section's own beat table, further down than I had read
# - and that table says explicitly that none of them is a data-file record:
# "An implementation cannot read these strings out of the user's data files;
# it has to carry them." All nine beats, their waits and the one blocking key
# are implemented now, in §7's "complete print-and-wait order".
